recipes.name: Egg Drop Soup (Better than Restaurant Quality!)

steps.text: Combine chicken broth, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a small saucepan over medium heat; bring to a boil.
Combine water and cornstarch in a small bowl until cornstarch is dissolved; stir into boiling broth. Stir in food coloring.
Slowly pour in beaten egg, stirring constantly in one direction to form thin egg ribbons. Season soup with white pepper and salt.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chives. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Egg Drop Soup (Better than Restaurant Quality!)
raw_recipe.description: This easy egg drop soup recipe is quick to make with pantry staples and a splash of sesame oil and soy sauce in just 10 minutes; faster than takeout.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make quick-and-easy egg drop soup. This simple soup is warm and soothing, and easily as good as what you’d get at Chinese restaurants.

review.reviewBody: Wow! This soup was quick and easy, and best of all, it tasted great. It is very creamy with the corn starch and ratio of 1 egg per cup of broth. Thank you for a delicious recipe!

Great recipe! The only thing I would change is the ground white pepper was way to much, try a 1/4 tsp of it. The 1/2 tsp made it a little too overpowering. But again, it does say optional. I loved the large amount of egg compared to the other egg drop soup recipes on this site.

In my mind this was just perfect, a delicious prelude to the Korean Saewoo Bokkeumbap (Shrimp Fried Rice) that followed it. (recipe also from this site) I don't know what it is, specifically, that makes this soup so good given its simplicity, but I can only guess it's the addition of the sesame oil, which I love. I prepared the recipe just as is, only mixing the cornstarch with part of the chicken broth rather than water and adding no salt or pepper. I made two servings, one serving each for Hubs and me, and regret I didn't make more. The consolation is that this is so quick and easy to prepare I could whip up more in no time!

Great recipe! The sesame oil that the recipe called for seemed like a lot to me so I just put a few drops in. I also don't use chicken broth (I never can get through it all in time), instead I used chicken bullion powder. Delicious!

Too good to only make 1 serving at a time and it scales up very easily. I used a 32 oz. carton of broth, 4 eggs, a teaspoon each of soy and sesame oil, and a tablespoon of corn starch with very good results. The scallions, salt and white pepper are also a must. Made as is, the recipe is absolutely fine. I might add some tofu next time for variety as I will certainly be making it again. Thanks for posting!

This has been my to-go for egg drop soup for a while now; thought a review was past due. I use consomme, leave out the salt and pepper. Add green onion at the end. The perfect ratio for us is one egg to two cups broth. I beat the eggs in a measuring cup and place the tings of a fork against the cup spout - keep moving as you slowly pour. The fork tings will ensure the egg does not go in clumpy.

OMG I am never buying egg drop soup from a restaurant again. So quick and easy to make with ingredients I always have on hand anyway. I skipped the cornstarch, food coloring, salt, and white pepper and it's still fabulous. I used 1 Goya powdered chicken bouillon packet, 2 cups water, 1 Goya salad & vegetable seasoning packet, 2 eggs , soy sauce, and my favorite sesame oil (which totally makes the soup!). I did NOT whisk the eggs into the broth, simply "dropped" them in like the name suggests so I got the nice long stringy egg pieces. Topped it with fresh chives and voila! Yummm...

I love it but 1400 mg of salt in one serving is MASSIVE. You realize your only supposed to eat 2000 a DAY. So half the chicken broth and low sodium at that for me. Also my wife is japanese and it's a sin to add sesame oil until your done cooking the food. Otherwise the oil just boils away and has no scent. Add oil after you turn off the stove and it's awesome! Thanks

I’ve been trying out different egg drop soup recipes over the past few weeks. This is definitely one of the better ones. Key to making the perfect egg ribbons is that this recipe has you use a pan instead of a pot. 

Deducted one star because it doesn’t include ginger. Most of the other recipes have it as an ingredient. I added a pinch of freshly grated ginger. I did not use food coloring.

This is my basic go to recipe for egg drop soup now. I made it the first time as written and it was really good. Since then I've made three changes. First I doubled the chicken broth because I like my egg drop soup a little thinner. Second, when I beat the eggs I add in a dollop of vegetable oil--that makes the eggs thread out better when I drizzle them into a rolling boil. Third, I add 2 teaspoons of cider vinegar to clarify the liquid which also adds just a bit of a tang to the soup.

This is a great start. First time I made it per the recipe. It was missing a little flavor. Second time with a couple tweaks was outstanding.
Based on using 2 cans of chicken broth:
I added half a large white onion sliced up and 4 Tbs. of Oigatsuo Tsuyu concentrated soup base. Brought it all to a boil, and kept low boiling until onions were almost translucent.
After those modifications, 5-star!
This is a wonderful recipe. I substituted shrimp stock for chicken stock and reduced the amount of pepper and we loved it!

This was a lifesaver for me today, as I’m following a bland diet after some GI issues. I needed something flavorful and this did the trick! It was incredibly easy and quite comforting, as well as tasty. I’ll be adding this to my regular lunch rotation, especially when it’s cooler out.

I've been making this this recipe for about six years since moving to the West Coast, where the egg drop soup is different and not as tasty as this version. Its easy to make and on a chilly day makes a good starter for lunch or dinner. I've given the recipe to several friends after they have had it at my house. One of our favorites.
easy and Delicious
Use vegetable bouillon for the broth, still delicious.
So easy to make and Delicious
None no changes
TOO MUCH PEPPER. really delicious and easy to make other than that. 👍

Wow, this is excellent! For someone with not much of an appetite this was a perfect meal! I did make some changes however to fit what I already had in my kitchen. I substituted sesame oil with canola oil, chicken stock with buijon cubes and white pepper with a smaller amount of black pepper. My whole family ate this up and I am surely making this again, without a doubt!
